meta.title: CZ-6A Launch visibility
notes: Provisional repeat-flight model, not an observed or uniquely determined trajectory. The March Yaogan-50 02 reconstruction and precursor orbit family supply conditional priors, not October observations or prediction confidence limits.

The dogleg is attributed to stage 1 and NOTAM A5283/26 to the booster drop zone. This is a stage-attribution correction only: the numerical surrogate's earlier staging boundary, thrust and steering assumptions were NOT refitted. No timed dogleg, staging, separation or impact event is claimed.
NOTAM 10:07–10:28 UTC is a hazard-area activation interval, not launch-time limits or an insertion constraint. The 09:30–11:00 UTC selector is an exploratory range, not an announced launch window.

Shifting T0 reuses the same Earth-fixed (ECEF) trajectory and changes the solar geometry; it does not reoptimize dynamics or propagate a newly fitted orbit. The nominal synthetic TLE remains a reference, not a new catalog observation.

Source positions and velocities use a TEME-like frame with GMST rotation, UTC approximating UT1 and no polar motion. The exporter converts to ECEF and resamples with cubic Hermite interpolation; it does not reoptimize or integrate a new trajectory.

The source dynamics include central gravity and J2, with a kinematic lower ascent and an assumed finite-thrust segment. Higher harmonics, post-insertion maneuvers, fragmentation and debris descent are not modeled.
Altitude samples are WGS84 geodetic ellipsoidal heights in km. Perigee and apogee are orbital radii minus the WGS84 equatorial radius; these are not the same altitude convention.
Sunlight uses the geometric Sun centre from the shared DE440s ephemeris and WGS84 ellipsoidal Earth occultation. The solar table is linearly interpolated in ECEF at 30-second cadence.

The 15° visibility envelope is sampled during sunlit ascent for sea-level observers with Sun-centre altitude ≤0°, then clipped to the observer night side at the insertion reference epoch. Post-insertion orbit tracks do not enlarge the ascent envelope.
No brightness, atmospheric refraction or extinction, weather, terrain, finite solar-disc emergence, or plume size is modeled. Geometric visibility is not a claim of naked-eye detection.
The 1.5 revolutions shown are exactly 1.5 times the insertion Keplerian period in elapsed time, not a claim of an exact J2 ground-track repeat or true-anomaly recurrence.
The synthetic prelaunch TLE uses placeholder catalog number 00000 and is explicitly NOT OBSERVED. It is fitted to the nominal numerical orbit; some TLE consumers reject this placeholder.

zones.desc: Booster drop zone; no impact trajectory or timing modeled
